messages.message: Hi Italy, let's start with a strong alliance. I'll move F TRI to ALB aiming for Greece, keeping my armies north in Serbia/Galicia direction. This leaves Venice safe. You can send F NAP to TUN unopposed. Together we crush Turkey - AI vs T. Deal?

Turkey, Russia starts with 4 SC and eyes the Black Sea. Let's ally against them: I'll take Serbia and support you into Bulgaria/Rumania. My fleet goes Albania-Greece. No attacks on your centers. Deal?
Russia, no need for early war. I'll focus south: F TRI to ALB, A BUD to SER, A VIE hold or TYR. You can take Rumania safely. Avoid GAL if possible. Let's both grow against others.
Germany, friendly neighbor. No moves to BOH from me. You focus west/north, I'll go southeast. Mutual non-aggression?

Greetings France. I am interested in a peaceful start to the game to avoid a costly early war in the English Channel. Would you be open to a DMZ in the English Channel (ENG) for the first few turns? This would allow us both to focus our expansion elsewhere.

Hello Germany. I'm looking to establish a stable relationship in the North. How do you view the situation regarding Belgium and Denmark? I am open to coordinating our moves to ensure we both grow efficiently without unnecessary conflict.
Greetings Russia. I hope for a peaceful North. Do you have any specific intentions regarding Norway, or shall we coordinate to ensure we don't clash there in the early stages?
Ciao Italia! France here. I'm looking to secure my western flank and expand south. Let's ensure our interests align in the Mediterranean and beyond. What are your initial thoughts?

Greetings England. France here. I'm focused on securing my immediate borders this year. Let's ensure our naval movements in the Channel are not misinterpreted. I'm open to discussing our mutual interests.
Hallo Deutschland. France here. Curious about your initial plans for the early game. Are you looking to focus east or west? I hope we can maintain a stable relationship.
Guten Tag Österreich. France here. I hope we can maintain a peaceful coexistence this year. What are your initial strategic considerations?
Здравствуйте Россия. France here. Just checking in to see your initial thoughts on the board. Hope for a stable start.
Merhaba Türkiye. France here. Wishing you a successful start to the year. What are your initial plans?
Austria, Germany values stability. Let us form an alliance to secure Central Europe. I propose we coordinate against Russia or France as we see fit.
France, Germany has no desire for war on the Rhine. Let us agree to hold our borders in 1901. We can discuss Belgium later.
Russia, Berlin is near Warsaw. Let us avoid conflict in Prussia. I propose a non-aggression pact to focus elsewhere.
Germany seeks stability in Europe. We are open to alliances but will defend our borders firmly.

Greetings Vienna. Italy is pushing south this year to secure Tunis and the Ionian. I propose we keep the Adriatic stable in 1901. If you focus your expansion toward the Balkans and Galicia, we can avoid a costly clash over Trieste. Let's coordinate to ensure neither of us is overextended early.

Salut Paris. Italy has no designs on Western Europe. My fleets and armies are moving aggressively into the Mediterranean and North Africa. I suggest we maintain a firm but peaceful border along the Alps. If you're looking to pressure Germany or England, I'll gladly stay out of your way in exchange for your neutrality in Piedmont and Tuscany.

Greetings Constantinople. The Mediterranean offers plenty of room for both of us. I intend to secure Tunis and Greece quickly. I propose we divide the eastern Med: I'll stay out of the Aegean and Black Sea if you respect my claims in the central Med. Open communication will prevent misunderstandings as we both expand.

Italy enters 1901 with clear objectives: securing the Mediterranean and expanding our influence. We value transparency and mutual non-aggression pacts. Powers looking to coordinate on neutral territories or secure their flanks are welcome to reach out. Let's make this a decisive year.

Greetings all. Russia seeks peaceful borders this year. I propose a non‑aggression pact with Austria, Germany, and Turkey. No moves into each other's home centers. Happy to discuss mutual support if needed.
Hello Austria, Russia would like to ensure stability in the east. I can offer support to your army in Budapest if you keep your forces away from Warsaw and Moscow. Let me know your thoughts.
Germany, a friendly stance would benefit us both. I can support your army in Berlin against any Austrian push, provided you respect our borders in Warsaw and St. Petersburg.
Turkey, Russia is interested in a mutual non‑aggression agreement. I have no plans to move toward Ankara or Constantinople, and I would appreciate the same from you.

Greetings Russia! As neighbors, I believe our relationship in the early game will define both our fortunes. I'd like to propose a Black Sea DMZ - neither of us moves there in Spring 1901. This builds trust between us and lets us both focus on expansion elsewhere. I'm looking south and west toward the Balkans, and have no designs on your territory. Would you be open to this arrangement? Perhaps we can even coordinate against Austria down the line.

Hello Austria! I think there's a natural opportunity for us to cooperate in the Balkans rather than clash. There are enough neutral supply centers for both of us to grow without stepping on each other's toes. I'm thinking I take Bulgaria and aim for Greece, while you focus on Serbia and Romania. Would you be interested in discussing a non-aggression arrangement? The real threats to both of us are Russia and Italy, not each other.

Greetings Italy! I wanted to reach out early since we're both Mediterranean powers with overlapping interests. I think we could benefit greatly from cooperation rather than competition. Austria sits between us and is a natural target for both - if we coordinate, we can carve up their territory effectively. In the short term, I'll be focused on the eastern Med and Balkans. Would you be interested in discussing a joint strategy?

Hello England! I know we're on opposite ends of the map, but that makes us natural allies - we can never directly threaten each other. I'd love to establish a long-term strategic partnership. If you're looking to pressure Russia from the north, I can keep them busy in the south. Let me know if you'd like to coordinate.

Hello Russia, I fully endorse your NAP proposal with Austria, Germany, and Turkey - no home center incursions, mutual growth. Privately, thanks for the support offer to Budapest. Agreed on eastern stability: I'll move F TRI - ALB (south to Balkans), A BUD - SER, A VIE - GAL (watching north but no further without coordination). This leaves Rumania open for you. Can you confirm avoiding Galicia to prevent a bounce? Let's both grab neutrals and prosper.

Turkey, excellent thinking - Russia and Italy are the real threats, not us. Non-aggression confirmed. Let's split the Balkans cleanly: you secure BUL and position for GRE, I'll take SER and RUM. My moves: A BUD - RUM, F TRI - ALB (flank support potential), A VIE - GAL (to pressure Russia). No issues with your centers. Coordinate after we both grow?

Italy, glad we're aligned. Confirmed: F TRI - ALB straight south for Greece (Adriatic untouched, Venice 100% safe), A BUD - SER, A VIE - GAL north. Your NAP to TUN unopposed. AI crushes Turkey - we split their centers next year. Deal locked?
Germany, mutual non-aggression solid. I'll expand southeast (Balkans), you handle west/north. No BOH moves from me. Let's monitor Russia/France together.

Hello Turkey! I completely agree—our distance is our greatest asset. I am very interested in a long-term strategic partnership. Let's coordinate our efforts to keep Russia contained. I'll be focusing on the North; it would be a huge help if you can keep them occupied in the south. Let's keep a close line of communication open.

France, thank you for the reply. To ensure there are no misinterpretations, I am proposing a formal DMZ in the English Channel (ENG) for this turn. If neither of us moves there, we both start the game with a clear signal of trust and can focus our units on other opportunities. Does this sound acceptable to you?

Hello Italy. I read your global message and appreciate your commitment to transparency. While we are far apart, I believe a mutual non-aggression pact would be beneficial for both of us to ensure stability while we expand. I'm happy to agree to such a pact.

Russia, I appreciate your overtures for peace. I am willing to honor a non-aggression pact regarding Warsaw and St. Petersburg. However, I must secure Silesia for my own defense. Your offer to support Berlin is noted, but I prefer mutual non-aggression over entanglement. Let us keep the East quiet.
Italy, your message is received. We share an interest in stability. Let us keep the Mediterranean open for cooperation and ensure no conflicts arise in our respective spheres.
Austria, your assurance on Bohemia is welcome. I will proceed to secure Bohemia. Let us ensure our southern flank remains stable and coordinate against common threats.
England, Denmark is a strategic necessity for Germany. I intend to move there. Belgium remains a topic for future discussion. Let us avoid naval conflict in the North Sea.

Constantinople, I appreciate the proposal. A coordinated pressure on Austria aligns perfectly with my long-term strategy. For 1901, I will secure Tunis and move into the Ionian to control the central Mediterranean. If you focus your efforts on Bulgaria and the Black Sea, we can effectively squeeze Austria from both flanks without overlapping. Let's maintain open communication and adjust our coordination as the board develops.

Berlin, I acknowledge your call for stability. Italy's ambitions are strictly focused on the Mediterranean and North Africa. I have zero interest in the Alpine border or German territories. A firm mutual non-aggression understanding would allow you to secure your western and northern fronts without diverting resources south. I propose we keep the Alps quiet and focus on our respective expansion zones.

St. Petersburg, your proposal for peaceful borders is well received. Italy's expansion is directed entirely southward into the Mediterranean and the Balkans. We have no conflicting interests in 1901, and I am fully prepared to respect your northern and eastern spheres of influence. I welcome a non-aggression understanding and look forward to keeping channels open as the game progresses.

Italy reaffirms its strategic focus on securing the Mediterranean basin and North Africa. We welcome bilateral discussions to define clear spheres of influence and prevent early conflicts. Stability in the north and west allows all powers to expand efficiently. Reach out if you wish to coordinate on neutral territories or establish mutual non-aggression terms.

Germany, I welcome your desire for stability. I agree to a non‑aggression pact respecting our borders in Warsaw, Prussia and the Baltic. In return I can offer a support hold for your army in Berlin this turn if you keep your forces away from Moscow and St. Petersburg. Let me know if this works for you.

Italy, thank you for the transparent approach. I have no immediate interest in the Mediterranean, so a mutual non‑aggression agreement sounds good. I will focus north and east, leaving the Balkans open for you. If you ever need support against Austria, feel free to ask.

Turkey, I accept the Black Sea DMZ for Spring 1901. Neither of us will move into the Black Sea or its adjacent coastal provinces (SEV, ANK, CON, SMY) this turn. This will help build trust and let us both expand elsewhere. I am also open to future coordination against Austria if our interests align.

Russia proposes a general non‑aggression understanding: no moves into each other's home centers this year, and a Black Sea DMZ with Turkey for Spring. I look forward to peaceful borders and possible support deals with any power that respects these terms.

Thank you for the reassurance. I'm fully committed to our Black Sea DMZ - I won't move F ANK to BLA this spring, and I trust you'll keep F SEV out as well. This lets both of us focus on more productive expansion. I'm heading into Bulgaria and the Balkans. If you're looking at Romania, perhaps we can coordinate so we don't trip over each other? A strong Russo-Turkish partnership can dominate the east.

I appreciate the proposal! I think we can work together very effectively. Here's what I'm thinking for Spring: I'll move A CON to Bulgaria and position my fleet to control the Black Sea, which puts pressure on Russia's southern flank. If you take Serbia and we coordinate in the fall, we can lock down the Balkans between us before Russia gets a foothold in Romania. One question - you mentioned Greece. I was actually eyeing Greece myself since Italy told me they want it, and I'd rather we take it than let Italy have it. Could we discuss who gets Greece? Romania might be a better fit for you given your position.

I appreciate the proposal on dividing the Mediterranean. I'm happy to stay out of the central Med - that's clearly your domain. However, I need to push back on Greece. Greece is directly adjacent to my position and is really in my natural sphere of expansion. If you take Tunis (which is right next door to you) and I take Greece, we both get a build without any friction. The Aegean is critical for my security, and having a foreign fleet near my waters would make me nervous. I think Tunis + working against Austria/France gives you plenty of growth without us clashing. What do you think?

Bonjour France! Thank you for reaching out. My initial plans are focused on the Balkans and eastern Mediterranean - Bulgaria, Greece, and keeping Russia honest. We're far enough apart that we should never conflict. I'd be very interested in a long-term partnership. If you're looking to expand east into Italy's territory eventually, I could help pressure Italy from the other side. For now, I'd love to exchange information about what you're hearing from other powers. Any intelligence on Italy's plans?

Just following up - I think a cross-map alliance between us could be very powerful. Neither of us can threaten the other, so there's zero trust risk. If you're planning to move against Russia (St. Petersburg is tempting, I'm sure), let me know and I can coordinate pressure from the south. Even if you're going west first, I'd appreciate any intel you pick up about Russia's intentions. Good luck this spring!

goals: Secure 2+ neutral SC in 1901F (SER, GRE/ALB support, RUM/BUL)
Build AI alliance vs Turkey or AT vs Russia based on Spring results
Grow to 5-6 SC by end-1901
Contain Russia (Gal pressure) and Germany (monitor Boh/Tyr)
Achieve 18 SC long-term via Balkan dominance
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] Tentative Balkan split with Turkey (me SER/RUM via Bud-Rum, them BUL/GRE; F Tri-Alb, Vie-Gal); AI vs Turkey proposal with Italy (Bud-Ser, Tri-Alb, Vie-Gal; Adriatic stable); NAP with Russia (no home centers, avoid Gal bounce, leave Rum open; support Bud offer); NNA with Germany (no Boh from me, they plan to take it); France neutral greeting. Conflicts: Bud-Ser (Italy) vs Bud-Rum (Turkey) vs Rum open (Russia). Russia proposed general NAP.
Intent: Aggressively expand south/east: F TRI - ALB (agreed all), A BUD - SER (Italy pref, safe vs Rum bounce risk; alt to Turkey Rum), A VIE - GAL (vs Russia, hope no bounce per NAP). Fulfil non-aggression; test trusts in Fall. No holds.

[S1901M] [S1901M Result] Perfect execution: TRI-ALB, BUD-SER, VIE-GAL all succeeded uncontested, securing SER (SC) and key footholds in ALB/GAL. Russia honored NAP (full holds, no GAL/RUM challenge), boosting trust. Turkey ignored Balkan split (consolidated ANK/BUL/CON instead of BUL/GRE push), missing RUM—opportunistic for me. Italy executed AI anti-Turkey plan (TYR/APU/ION), but TYR eyes VIE—watch closely. Germany standard (BOH/SIL/DEN), no NNA violation. No betrayals; all collaborations held (Russia NAP, Italy coord). Position strengthened: 3 aggressive units, poised for 2+ SC (SER + GRE/RUM/BUL via ALB/SER/GAL). Lesson: Russia reliable short-term; pivot to AI vs Turkey for Fall builds to 5-6 SC. Contain ITA TYR, probe Turkey weakness. Aggressive east/south continues.

goals: Secure Norway in S1901M
Establish a stable relationship with France via the ENG DMZ
Coordinate with Turkey to contain Russia
Avoid early conflict with Germany in the North Sea
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] France is non-committal regarding the English Channel (ENG) DMZ, though not explicitly hostile. Germany intends to take Denmark and wants to avoid naval conflict in the North Sea. Turkey has proposed a strong cross-map alliance to pressure Russia. Italy has agreed to a mutual non-aggression pact.
Intent: I intend to move F LON to North Sea, F EDI to Norway, and A LVP to Yorkshire. I will avoid moving into the English Channel to signal trust to France and adhere to the spirit of the proposed DMZ. I will take Norway despite Germany's move to Denmark to ensure my own expansion.

[S1901M] S1901M was a successful opening. I secured Norway and established a presence in the North Sea. France respected the English Channel DMZ, signaling a willingness to cooperate, which stabilizes my southern flank. Germany took Denmark as expected, and we currently coexist peacefully in the North. The most shocking development is Russia's total passivity; holding all units in the first turn is an unprecedented waste of tempo. This makes Russia an incredibly vulnerable target and significantly strengthens the strategic value of my alliance with Turkey. My position is strong, and the balance of power in the north has shifted in my favor. I will continue to maintain the peace with France and Germany while coordinating with Turkey to exploit Russia's inexplicable stagnation.

goals: Achieve world domination by controlling 18 supply centers.
Secure immediate western and southern borders while expanding aggressively.
Establish a strong foothold in the English Channel and potentially the North Sea.
Maintain flexibility for future alliances and opportunistic gains.
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England proposed an English Channel DMZ, to which France responded non-committally, indicating a focus on securing borders and open discussion. Italy proposed a non-aggression pact along the Alps, with Italy focusing on the Mediterranean and North Africa, and encouraging France to pressure Germany or England. Germany proposed holding borders on the Rhine in 1901. Turkey expressed interest in a long-term partnership, suggesting future cooperation against Italy and focusing on the Balkans/Eastern Med. France has not explicitly agreed to any DMZs or non-aggression pacts, maintaining flexibility for aggressive expansion.
Intent: France will pursue aggressive expansion in S1901M. A MAR will move to Piedmont (PIE) to secure southern expansion, aligning with Italy's stated focus on the Mediterranean and their proposal for a peaceful Alps border. A PAR will move to Burgundy (BUR) to pressure Germany's eastern flank, respecting Germany's desire for no war on the Rhine. F BRE will move to the Mid-Atlantic Ocean (MAO) to begin pressuring England and securing northern expansion, as France did not formally agree to England's DMZ proposal and aims to expand aggressively.

[S1901M] England has proven untrustworthy, breaking their Channel DMZ proposal and moving F LON to NTH. Our F BRE to MAO was a necessary counter. England is now our primary western threat. Italy is cooperating as planned, securing our southern border with their moves to ION. Germany is looking east, not west, with A MUN to BOH and A BER to SIL, leaving A PAR's move to BUR as a good pressure point on their eastern flank. All our units moved successfully. We must now focus on containing and dismantling England's northern fleet.

goals: Secure Bohemia, Silesia, and Denmark in 1901
Maintain alliance with Austria against Russia/France
Reach 6 supply centers by end of 1901
Prepare for potential conflict with France or Russia in 1902
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] Austria agreed to mutual non-aggression and ceded BOH to Germany in exchange for German focus on West/North. Russia agreed to NAG on WAR/STP borders, permitting German expansion into SIE. England acknowledged German claim on DEN and agreed to avoid North Sea conflict. France and Italy agreed to border stability and non-aggression.
Intent: Execute aggressive expansion: A MUN to BOH (per Austria agreement), A BER to SIE (per Russia NAG), F KIE to DEN (per England acknowledgment). No holds. Secure 3 new SCs.

[S1901M] Spring 1901 was a flawless execution. All three expansion orders succeeded: A MUN to BOH, A BER to SIL, and F KIE to DEN. Austria honored the peace pact by vacating Bohemia, Russia held on the eastern border allowing Silesia, and England did not contest Denmark. No betrayals occurred; all initial agreements were respected. Germany now controls 6 supply centers, doubling our starting strength. This establishes a dominant position in Central Europe and the North Sea. Austria and Russia appear reliable allies for now, though Russia's passive hold suggests caution. England's neutrality in the North is beneficial. With 6 SCs, we are ahead of schedule. Next phase, I must consolidate these gains and prepare for potential friction with France or Russia in 1902. The alliance network holds, but vigilance is required as power balances shift.

goals: Secure Tunis and build a second fleet in 1901
Establish control over the Ionian Sea and prepare for Greek expansion
Maintain peaceful Alpine/Adriatic borders to focus resources south
Coordinate with Austria to pressure Turkey and split Balkan centers
Expand aggressively to reach 18 supply centers for world domination
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] Austria confirmed F TRI-ALB, A BUD-SER, A VIE-GAL, leaving Adriatic stable and expecting Italy to take TUN for joint anti-Turkey strategy. Turkey conceded TUN to Italy but firmly claims Greece; proposed coordinated pressure on Austria. Russia, England, and Germany all agreed to mutual non-aggression/stability pacts, with Russia explicitly leaving Balkans open and offering future support vs Austria. France remains open to peaceful Alpine border. Overall, strong diplomatic foundation for southern expansion with minimal northern friction.
Intent: F NAP -> TUN (fulfilling agreement with Austria/Turkey to secure North Africa unopposed). A VEN -> TYR (secures northern flank, respects Austrian/German borders, avoids early Alpine conflict). A ROM -> APU (positions aggressively for Ionian Sea control and future Greek/Balkan operations). All units ordered aggressively southward/northeastward to maximize expansion potential while honoring diplomatic assurances.

[S1901M] S1901M executed mostly as planned, but I critically failed to secure TUN; F NAP moved to ION instead, costing me a vital free build and delaying North African consolidation. Austria honored all commitments, solidifying our Balkan/Adriatic understanding. However, France’s A MAR-PIE move directly violates our peaceful Alpine understanding and threatens my northern flank. I must immediately reinforce TYR or negotiate a firm border to prevent early French aggression. Russia’s passive holds and Turkey’s consolidation in BUL/CON align with expectations, leaving the Ionian and Aegean open for my next push. Strategic lesson: verify unit orders against diplomatic promises before submission, and never assume French neutrality without concrete guarantees. Next phase priority: secure TUN with F ION, monitor French PIE closely, and prepare to contest Greece while maintaining Austrian cooperation.

goals: Secure RUM in Spring 1901 and later expand into the Balkans.
Maintain peaceful borders with Austria, Germany, Turkey and Italy.
Build a strong presence in the Black Sea region while respecting the DMZ.
Reach 18 supply centers for world domination.
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] Russia has secured a general non‑aggression pact with Austria, Germany, Turkey and Italy: no moves into each other's home centers this year. Austria will move F TRI → ALB, A BUD → SER, A VIE → GAL and leaves RUM open for Russia; Russia will avoid GAL to prevent a bounce. Turkey and Russia agree to a Black Sea DMZ for Spring 1901 (no moves into SEV, ANK, CON, SMY). No other powers have made concrete agreements.
Intent: Russia will honor the agreements: A WAR will not move into GAL; instead it will move to UKR (support possible) or hold. A MOS will hold or move to UKR to prepare for RUM. F SEV will hold (respecting Black Sea DMZ). F STP/SC will hold. No orders will target Austria, Germany, Turkey, Italy home centers or Black Sea provinces.

[S1901M] Russia kept its word: all four units held, respecting the Black‑Sea DMZ and the non‑aggression pact. Austria honored the agreement, moving its fleet to ALB and armies to SER and GAL, leaving RUM open as promised. Turkey also kept the DMZ, shifting CON→BUL, ANK→CON and SMY→ANK without touching SEV. Germany, England, France and Italy made no moves that threatened us, so the pact held across the board. No betrayals occurred this turn, which is a rare clean spring. The hold orders leave us perfectly positioned to push into RUM next season, then swing into GAL or BUD without fear of a bounce. Trustworthiness appears high among Austria and Turkey, moderate with Germany and England, and neutral with France and Italy. Lesson: honor our own commitments; it builds reciprocal restraint and buys us the time needed to expand into the Balkans and secure the Black Sea foothold.

[S1901M] Russia has secured a general non‑aggression pact with Austria, Germany, Turkey and Italy: no moves into each other's home centers this year. Austria will move F TRI → ALB, A BUD → SER, A VIE → GAL and leaves RUM open for Russia; Russia will avoid GAL to prevent a bounce. Turkey and Russia agree to a Black Sea DMZ for Spring 1901 (no moves into SEV, ANK, CON, SMY). No other powers have made concrete agreements.
Intent: Russia will honor the agreements: A WAR will not move into GAL; instead it will move to UKR (support possible) or hold. A MOS will hold or move to UKR to prepare for RUM. F SEV will hold (respecting Black Sea DMZ). F STP/SC will hold. No orders will target Austria, Germany, Turkey, Italy home centers or Black Sea provinces.

[S1901M] Russia kept its word: all four units held, respecting the Black‑Sea DMZ and the non‑aggression pact. Austria honored the agreement, moving its fleet to ALB and armies to SER and GAL, leaving RUM open as promised. Turkey also kept the DMZ, shifting CON→BUL, ANK→CON and SMY→ANK without touching SEV. Germany, England, France and Italy made no moves that threatened us, so the pact held across the board. No betrayals occurred this turn, which is a rare clean spring. The hold orders leave us perfectly positioned to push into RUM next season, then swing into GAL or BUD without fear of a bounce. Trustworthiness appears high among Austria and Turkey, moderate with Germany and England, and neutral with France and Italy. Lesson: honor our own commitments; it builds reciprocal restraint and buys us the time needed to expand into the Balkans and secure the Black Sea foothold.

goals: Secure Bulgaria in Spring 1901
Take Greece in Fall 1901 - position fleet through Aegean
Honor Black Sea DMZ with Russia in Spring to build trust
Maintain Austrian alliance - coordinate Balkan division
Block Italy from Greece - this is MY supply center
Keep Russia friendly but prepare contingency if they betray DMZ
Long-term: dominate eastern Mediterranean and Balkans, then expand toward Russia or Austria when the time is right
Leverage England alliance for intelligence and coordinated anti-Russian pressure
Build 1-2 units in Fall 1901 (fleet preferred for Mediterranean expansion)

[S1901M] Key agreements: (1) AUSTRIA - Allied against Russia/Italy. Split Balkans: I get BUL and GRE, Austria gets SER and RUM. Austria plans A BUD-RUM, F TRI-ALB, A VIE-GAL. Non-aggression confirmed. (2) RUSSIA - Black Sea DMZ agreed for Spring 1901. Neither moves to BLA. I committed F ANK won't go to BLA, Russia keeps F SEV out. Discussed future coordination against Austria (contradicts my Austrian alliance - I'm keeping options open). (3) ITALY - Tension over Greece. Italy wants Tunis AND Greece. I pushed back hard, claiming Greece as my sphere. Italy plans F NAP-ION and securing Tunis. We discussed vague anti-Austrian coordination but nothing firm. (4) ENGLAND - Long-range alliance to contain Russia. They focus north, I pressure south. Zero conflict risk. (5) FRANCE - Brief exchange. I hinted at future anti-Italy coordination. No concrete deals. (6) GERMANY - No direct communication.
Intent: Honor the Black Sea DMZ with Russia. Moves: A CON-BUL (secure Bulgaria), F ANK-CON (position fleet for Aegean/Greece in Fall), A SMY-ANK (reposition army). Fall plan: F CON-AEG to target Greece, potentially A BUL supports or moves to GRE. I am NOT moving to BLA this turn as promised to Russia. Priority is securing BUL and positioning for GRE.

[S1901M] All my moves succeeded perfectly - BUL secured, fleet positioned in CON, army ready in ANK. Black Sea DMZ honored by both sides. Austria executed exactly as promised (SER, ALB, GAL) - trust fully confirmed.

MAJOR SURPRISE: Russia held ALL four units. Completely passive. Either technical failure, paralysis by analysis, or deliberate sandbagging. This makes Russia look vulnerable - Germany's A SIL and A BOH combined with Austria's A GAL create enormous pressure on Russian positions.

CRITICAL THREAT: Italy moved F NAP-ION as feared. Combined with A APU, Italy is clearly positioning for Greece. This makes Fall timing essential - I MUST play F CON-AEG immediately. May need Austria's F ALB support to guarantee Greece against Italian competition.

POSITIVE: France moved A MAR-PIE, directly threatening Italy. This could distract Italian resources westward.

UPDATED ASSESSMENTS: Austria = highly trustworthy ally. Russia = enigma, possibly weak. Italy = confirmed rival for Greece. Germany = aggressively anti-Russia/Austria.

FALL PRIORITY: F CON-AEG, coordinate with Austria to secure Greece before Italy. Explore whether Russia's passivity creates expansion opportunities in Black Sea region for 1902.

messages.message: Perfect proposal—let's lock it in! I'll handle Romania for us: A GAL - RUM, A SER H (securing it), and F ALB S A BUL - GRE to support your advance into Greece. You go A BUL - GRE, and we split Balkans cleanly (you BUL/GRE, me SER/RUM). Russia gets nothing, we both build 2 units, and dominate east together. Confirm your other moves stay north (ANK hold, F CON - BLA for Black Sea pressure)? Long-term alliance vs Russia/Italy.

Agreed on spheres and NNA—stability north/west is key. I'll focus Balkans (SER secure, pushing RUM vs Russia/Turkey), you take Med/N Africa (TUN from ION, etc.). Anti-Turkey coord possible: my F ALB eyes ION/GRE pressure, your ION/APU/TYR set up nicely. Watch Germany BOH/TYR—joint defense if they push VIE? Let's grow together to 5+ SC this year.

NNA accepted—no home center threats this year, peaceful borders. My GAL - RUM pressures Turkey (not you), SER holds, ALB supports south. Black Sea DMZ good with Turkey. Possible mutual support vs Germany/Turkey later? Your holds honored trust—let's both expand safely.

I appreciate your proposal for non-aggression. However, given the current board state, I cannot overlook the opportunity to secure Norway. I intend to move there this fall. That said, I have no desire for a total war with Russia and would be open to discussing a more formal border agreement once my position in the north is stabilized.

Russia's total passivity in the spring was a shocking turn of events. I am moving to secure Norway this fall. I fully support the cross-map alliance; as you pressure them from the south, I will be in a position to look toward St. Petersburg. Let's keep our communication open to coordinate the timing of our advances.

I am pleased that we both respected the English Channel DMZ in the spring. I intend to continue focusing my efforts northward for the time being, and I hope we can maintain this stability to ensure our mutual growth.

I see you've secured Denmark. I'm moving into Norway this fall. As long as we both avoid naval conflict in the North Sea and respect each other's spheres of influence, I believe we can both expand efficiently.

I agree with your assessment. A stable north and west allows us all to expand. I accept your proposal for mutual non-aggression and look forward to hearing how your efforts in the Mediterranean progress.

Ciao Italia,

Thank you for your message. I agree that stability is key for efficient expansion, and I appreciate your focus on the Mediterranean and North Africa. My own immediate plans are concentrated on securing my western and northern borders. I'm keeping my options open for now, but I'm happy to discuss spheres of influence further as the game progresses. What are your thoughts on potential moves into Spain or North Africa this year?

Bonjour Turkey,

It's good to hear from you. I share your interest in a long-term partnership and agree that our powers are well-positioned to avoid conflict. My focus is indeed on the west and north, particularly dealing with England. Italy has indicated a strong focus on the Mediterranean and North Africa, which aligns with their message to me. I'm not planning any immediate moves towards Italy's territory, but I'm always open to exploring opportunities. What are your immediate plans regarding Russia and Austria?

Greetings Russia,

Thank you for proposing a non-aggression understanding. I can confirm that France has no intention of moving into your home centers this year, and I appreciate the gesture of peaceful borders. My current strategic focus is on the western and northern fronts, so your proposal does not conflict with my immediate plans. I wish you success in your diplomatic efforts.

France is focused on securing its western and northern borders this year. We are open to discussions regarding spheres of influence and maintaining stability, but aggressive expansion is our priority. We will not be drawn into unnecessary conflicts on our eastern flank.

We accept the Non-Aggression Pact. Germany respects the borders at Warsaw and St. Petersburg. We will not move into your home centers this year. In return, we expect no Russian moves into Silesia or Berlin. This stability allows us to focus our expansion towards the West and North Sea.

We acknowledge your strategic focus on the Mediterranean. Germany has no interest in the Mediterranean basin and will respect your sphere of influence there. We focus on Central Europe and the North. Peaceful borders are in our mutual interest.

Bohemia is secured as agreed. We value our alliance. Let's ensure our units in Galicia and Bohemia do not bounce in Fall. We are ready to coordinate our 1902 expansion plans to counterbalance France and Russia.

Turkey, I appreciate your transparency regarding Greece. I agree to your proposal: I will secure Tunis, and you may take Greece. This division gives us both a build and avoids unnecessary friction in the Mediterranean. I have no interest in the Aegean and will keep my fleet focused on North Africa and the Ionian. Let's maintain this understanding and coordinate against any power that threatens our respective spheres.

Russia, thank you for the clear non-aggression terms and the Black Sea DMZ proposal. I fully respect these boundaries and will keep my focus southward. I appreciate your offer of future support and will reciprocate with transparency. Let's maintain open communication as the board develops.

France, I noticed your army moved into Piedmont this spring. While I value peaceful relations, Piedmont serves as a critical buffer for my northern flank. I strongly request that you withdraw to Marseille or at least hold your position. Further advances into my territory will force me to reconsider our diplomatic stance and potentially align with other powers to secure my borders. I hope we can maintain a stable Alpine frontier.

Austria, our cooperation in the Balkans and Adriatic remains a top priority for me. I'm securing Tunis this fall as planned. I also want to flag France's move into Piedmont, which threatens our shared northern stability. I'd appreciate your continued support in keeping the Adriatic secure, and I'm open to discussing how we can jointly manage any French or German overreach. Let's keep our alliance strong.

Dear Italy, thank you for your friendly notes. I fully support our mutual non‑aggression understanding. Your focus on the Mediterranean and the Balkans aligns well with our eastern plans. Let us keep clear lines: you may advance into the Adriatic and the Italian peninsula, while I will look toward RUM and Romania. Should any neutral province (e.g., VEN, TYR, or the Balkans) become contested, we can discuss a simple split to avoid a bounce. I look forward to a stable north‑west for both of us.

Esteemed Turkey, I appreciate your commitment to the Black Sea DMZ. I will keep F SEV in place this spring, and I trust you will respect the same. Regarding Romania, I propose that we each respect the other's sphere: I will move toward RUM and then into ROM, while you may consider advancing into BUL or CON as you see fit. If any conflict over ROM arises, we can negotiate a peaceful hand‑off. Let us maintain this partnership to dominate the east.

Russia reaffirms the non‑aggression pact with Austria, Germany, Turkey and Italy for this year. All parties have agreed to respect each other's home centers and to observe the Black Sea DMZ. I will hold my units this turn and look forward to a cooperative expansion in the coming seasons.

Friend, excellent execution in Spring! Our coordination is paying off perfectly - you have Serbia, I have Bulgaria, just as planned.

CRITICAL ISSUE: Italy moved F NAP-ION and A ROM-APU. They are clearly targeting Greece. I plan to move F CON-AEG and A BUL-GRE this fall to secure it before Italy can. 

Can your F ALB support my A BUL-GRE? This would guarantee Greece falls to me regardless of what Italy does from ION. In return, Romania is yours for the taking - Russia held ALL units (bizarre, right?), meaning RUM is completely undefended.

Also - did you notice Russia's total passivity? All four units held. This is either a massive miscalculation or they're planning something unusual. Germany's A SIL and A BOH combined with your A GAL create enormous pressure. We should discuss exploiting this in 1902.

What's your Fall plan?

Russia, thank you for honoring the Black Sea DMZ - I noticed you kept F SEV in place and I kept my fleet away from BLA as promised. Trust confirmed on both sides.

I want to continue our peaceful relationship into Fall and beyond. My fleet is moving toward the Aegean to contest Italy's aggressive push into the eastern Mediterranean (they moved to ION, clearly eyeing Greece). My focus remains south and west, not north.

Question: I noticed you held all units in Spring. Are you facing pressure from Germany? Their moves to Bohemia and Silesia looked aggressive. If Germany is threatening you, I may be able to help diplomatically through my English contacts - England and I have been discussing containing German ambitions.

Shall we extend the Black Sea DMZ through Fall 1901 as well? I have no designs on the Black Sea this turn.

Italy, let me be direct with you. I see your fleet in ION and army in Apulia. I understand you want Tunis - that's perfectly reasonable and I have no objection.

However, Greece is in my sphere of influence. My army is already in Bulgaria, adjacent to Greece, and I have fleet support positioning through the Aegean. Austria's fleet in Albania also supports MY claim to Greece, not yours.

If you contest Greece, you will lose - and you'll also lose Tunis because your fleet will be tied up in a fight you can't win. That's bad for both of us.

Here's my proposal: You take Tunis (uncontested), I take Greece (uncontested). We establish a clear eastern Mediterranean boundary. Then in 1902, we can discuss whether Austria is getting too strong and coordinate accordingly. That's a much better deal than fighting over scraps while France moves A PIE against you.

Speak plainly - do we have an agreement?

England! Good Spring for both of us. Your northern positioning looks strong.

Intelligence update: Russia held ALL FOUR units in Spring. Every single one. F SEV stayed put, A WAR stayed put, everything held. This is extraordinary - either something went very wrong for them technically, or they're paralyzed. Germany moved aggressively toward Russia (A SIL, A BOH), so perhaps Russia is facing pressure they can't figure out how to respond to.

Meanwhile, Italy is making aggressive moves toward Greece (F ION, A APU). I'm positioning to block them and secure Greece myself.

Are you in contact with Germany? Their anti-Russian positioning is interesting. If Russia continues to be passive, there may be opportunities for coordinated pressure in 1902. I can threaten from the Black Sea, you from the north, Germany from the west.

What are your Fall plans?

France - I noticed your bold move to Piedmont. Very interesting! Italy moved aggressively eastward (F ION, A APU targeting Greece, A VEN-TYR), leaving their homeland exposed to you.

I'm currently in a contest with Italy over Greece. If you keep pressure on Italy from the west, it helps both of us - Italy can't fight a two-front war effectively. I'll tie up their eastern ambitions while you exploit their western vulnerability.

Would you be interested in coordinating anti-Italian strategy? Even if it's just maintaining pressure to keep them honest, it serves both our interests.

Friend, locked in! F ALB supports A BUL - GRE (guarantees vs Italy ION). A GAL - RUM (wide open), A SER holds SER. Confirm your A BUL - GRE, F CON - AEG (block ION?), A ANK holds? Russia holding all units again—insane passivity, perfect for us. We both build: me +2 (SER/RUM), you +1 (GRE, BUL move secures it?). AT dominates Balkans 1902 vs Russia/Italy. Execute!

Alliance strong, Adriatic fully secure—F ALB focused south (Balkans pressure, no threat to you). France PIE is bold overreach, Germany BOH/TYR pressuring VIE—agree on joint watch. You nail TUN from ION (easy), I'll secure RUM/SER. Growth first: you Med, me Balkans. Anti-Turkey if they push too hard? Coord Fall results.

I am indeed in contact with Germany, and I find their anti-Russian positioning very encouraging. My Fall plan is to secure Norway. Once that is settled, I am fully committed to our cross-map coordination. With Russia's current paralysis, the opportunity to squeeze them from the north while you pressure from the south is too good to pass up. Let's keep our communication open as we move into 1902.

Germany acknowledges your move to Norway. We confirm our commitment to North Sea stability. Denmark is secure, and we will not contest your expansion northward. Let us maintain this understanding to avoid unnecessary naval conflict.

We respect your focus on the West. Germany seeks stability on the Rhine. We will not move into Burgundy or Belgium, but we expect the same courtesy. Aggression here would force a difficult response. Let us keep our borders peaceful.

Turkey, I accept your proposal. I will secure Tunis uncontested this fall, and I acknowledge your claim to Greece for now. This clear division ensures we both gain a vital build and avoids unnecessary friction. I will keep my fleet focused on North Africa and the Ionian. Let's maintain this understanding and coordinate against any power that threatens our respective spheres.

Russia, thank you for reaffirming our non-aggression pact and the Black Sea DMZ. I fully respect these boundaries and will keep my focus southward. I appreciate your offer of future support and will reciprocate with transparency. Let's maintain open communication as the board develops.

Austria, our cooperation remains a top priority. I am securing Tunis this fall as planned. I must flag France's move into Piedmont, which threatens our shared northern stability. I'd appreciate your continued support in keeping the Adriatic secure, and I'm open to discussing how we can jointly manage any French or German overreach. Let's keep our alliance strong.

Dear Turkey,

I appreciate your continued respect for the Black Sea DMZ. Extending the DMZ through Fall 1901 is perfectly fine with me; I will keep my fleet in Sevastopol and will not move into the Black Sea provinces. Let us keep this mutual understanding to avoid any accidental clashes.

Best regards,
Russia

Hello Germany,

Thank you for reaffirming the non‑aggression pact. I have no intention of moving into Silesia or Berlin this year, and I will keep my armies on Warsaw, Moscow and St. Petersburg defensive. In return, I would appreciate that you continue to respect my borders in Galicia and the Baltic region. This stability allows me to focus on securing RUM and the Balkans as planned.

Regards,
Russia

Hi Italy,

Your commitment to the Black Sea DMZ and the non‑aggression terms is noted. I will hold my units this turn and aim for RUM in the fall, then possibly move toward Romania. Please continue to keep your focus on the Mediterranean; I have no interest in your home centers. Let us stay in touch about any contested neutral provinces in the Balkans.

Cheers,
Russia

Our spring agreement worked well. I will honor the pact in the fall as well and will not move into Galicia or Budapest. My next target is RUM, after which I may consider a move toward Galicia if the situation permits. I am open to discussing coordinated support against any common threats, should they arise.

Sincerely,
Russia

Italy, I'm glad we've reached a clear understanding. You take Tunis, I take Greece - clean, efficient, and no wasted energy fighting each other. I'll move through the Aegean to secure Greece this fall.

I'll honor this boundary going forward. The eastern Mediterranean is mine, North Africa and the western Med are yours. If we both build this year (which we should), we'll be in strong positions heading into 1902.

One thought for the future: Austria is expanding quickly in the Balkans. If they grow too powerful, we may need to coordinate. But that's a conversation for later. For now, let's both secure our builds.

Russia, absolutely - the Black Sea DMZ continues through Fall 1901. My fleet is moving toward the Aegean Sea to contest Italy's presence in the eastern Mediterranean, not toward the Black Sea. You can verify this at resolution.

Regarding Romania - I should be transparent with you. My focus this fall is entirely on Greece (army from Bulgaria moves south). I have no claims on Romania. However, I'd encourage you to move quickly on Romania if you want it - I've heard rumors that others may have designs on it given its undefended status. Don't let your passivity from Spring cost you a build.

Looking ahead to 1902: once I've secured Greece and you've secured your builds, we should discuss how the board develops. Germany's positioning (Silesia, Bohemia) looks threatening to both Austria and you. Thoughts?

Austria - confirmed! Here's my Fall plan:

- A BUL → GRE (please support with F ALB S A BUL - GRE)
- F CON → AEG (positioning for Mediterranean control)
- A ANK → ARM (positioning for future Black Sea pressure against Russia in 1902)

Good news: Italy has explicitly agreed to take Tunis and leave Greece to me. So the F ALB support is likely insurance rather than necessity, but let's guarantee it.

Also good news: Russia just messaged me reaffirming they'll hold AGAIN this fall. Romania should be completely free for your A GAL-RUM. Russia is essentially gifting us both builds.

For 1902: with you at 5 centers (SER, RUM + home 3) and me at 5 (BUL, GRE + home 3), we'll be the strongest alliance on the board. Then we turn on Russia together. My A ARM will be perfectly positioned to threaten Sevastopol. Your A GAL can pressure Warsaw/Ukraine. Beautiful coordination.

Confirm the F ALB support?

England - excellent, Norway should be an easy grab for you.

Update from my end: Russia just messaged me saying they intend to HOLD ALL UNITS AGAIN this fall. Confirmed in their global message too. This is remarkable - they're essentially surrendering tempo. Romania will likely fall to Austria, and the neutral centers around Russia are being absorbed by others.

I'm securing Greece this fall and positioning an army toward Armenia for 1902 Black Sea pressure. If Russia continues this passive strategy, they'll be surrounded and weakened by Spring 1902 without having gained anything.

Question: what's Germany telling you? Their moves to Silesia and Bohemia are extremely aggressive toward Russia (and arguably Austria). Are they coordinating with you, or acting independently? Understanding Germany's intent helps me plan whether Russia will be squeezed from all sides or just some.

Grab Norway and let's plan the 1902 campaign against Russia together.

full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England proposed an English Channel DMZ, to which France responded non-committally, indicating a focus on securing borders and open discussion. Italy proposed a non-aggression pact along the Alps, with Italy focusing on the Mediterranean and North Africa, and encouraging France to pressure Germany or England. Germany proposed holding borders on the Rhine in 1901. Turkey expressed interest in a long-term partnership, suggesting future cooperation against Italy and focusing on the Balkans/Eastern Med. France has not explicitly agreed to any DMZs or non-aggression pacts, maintaining flexibility for aggressive expansion.
Intent: France will pursue aggressive expansion in S1901M. A MAR will move to Piedmont (PIE) to secure southern expansion, aligning with Italy's stated focus on the Mediterranean and their proposal for a peaceful Alps border. A PAR will move to Burgundy (BUR) to pressure Germany's eastern flank, respecting Germany's desire for no war on the Rhine. F BRE will move to the Mid-Atlantic Ocean (MAO) to begin pressuring England and securing northern expansion, as France did not formally agree to England's DMZ proposal and aims to expand aggressively.

[S1901M] England has proven untrustworthy, breaking their Channel DMZ proposal and moving F LON to NTH. Our F BRE to MAO was a necessary counter. England is now our primary western threat. Italy is cooperating as planned, securing our southern border with their moves to ION. Germany is looking east, not west, with A MUN to BOH and A BER to SIL, leaving A PAR's move to BUR as a good pressure point on their eastern flank. All our units moved successfully. We must now focus on containing and dismantling England's northern fleet.

[F1901M] England proposed a Channel DMZ, which France did not commit to. England then moved F LON to NTH, breaking the DMZ, while France moved F BRE to MAO as a counter. England's subsequent message claims the DMZ was respected and seeks future stability, which is disingenuous. Italy proposed an Alps non-aggression pact, which France acknowledged while keeping options open. However, Italy now views France's A MAR to PIE move as hostile and demands withdrawal, threatening to reconsider diplomacy. Germany proposed a Rhine DMZ, which France accepted by agreeing not to move into Belgium or Burgundy, and Germany reciprocated. Turkey proposed an anti-Italian alliance, which France is open to, seeing an opportunity to exploit Italy's western vulnerability while Turkey engages them in the East. Russia proposed a non-aggression pact, which France accepted, confirming no intent to move into Russian home centers.
Intent: France will pursue aggressive expansion against England and Italy. F MAO will move to North Sea (NTH) to engage England's fleet. A PIE will move to Liguria (LIG) to pressure Italy's northern coast, capitalizing on Italy's hostility and Turkey's request for coordinated anti-Italian action. A PAR will move to Burgundy (BUR) to maintain pressure on Germany's eastern flank, as per previous intent, while respecting Germany's stated desire for border stability. A MAR will move to Piedmont (PIE) to support A PIE's advance or cover the southern border, given Italy's aggressive stance.

[F1901M] England broke their Channel DMZ proposal by moving F LON to NTH, confirming them as our primary western threat. France's F MAO to NAO move was a direct counter, though it did not immediately engage England's fleet as intended. Italy's hostile reaction to our A PIE move, demanding withdrawal, has solidified them as an enemy, aligning with Turkey's anti-Italian stance. Germany's Rhine border remains stable, with our A BUR move pressuring their eastern flank. Russia remains an ally. The key lesson is that England is untrustworthy and must be dealt with decisively. Italy's aggression requires immediate attention, potentially diverting resources from England. Our southern expansion into PIE was successful, but Italy's reaction was more severe than anticipated.

Intent: Russia will honor the agreements: A WAR will not move into GAL; instead it will move to UKR (support possible) or hold. A MOS will hold or move to UKR to prepare for RUM. Lesson: honor our own commitments; it builds reciprocal restraint and buys us the time needed to expand into the Balkans and secure the Black Sea foothold.

goals: Secure Norway
Capture St. Petersburg
Maintain stability with France and Germany
Coordinate with Turkey and Germany to dismantle Russia
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] France is non-committal regarding the English Channel (ENG) DMZ, though not explicitly hostile. Germany intends to take Denmark and wants to avoid naval conflict in the North Sea. Turkey has proposed a strong cross-map alliance to pressure Russia. Italy has agreed to a mutual non-aggression pact.
Intent: I intend to move F LON to North Sea, F EDI to Norway, and A LVP to Yorkshire. I will avoid moving into the English Channel to signal trust to France and adhere to the spirit of the proposed DMZ. I will take Norway despite Germany's move to Denmark to ensure my own expansion.

[S1901M] S1901M was a successful opening. I secured Norway and established a presence in the North Sea. France respected the English Channel DMZ, signaling a willingness to cooperate, which stabilizes my southern flank. Germany took Denmark as expected, and we currently coexist peacefully in the North. The most shocking development is Russia's total passivity; holding all units in the first turn is an unprecedented waste of tempo. This makes Russia an incredibly vulnerable target and significantly strengthens the strategic value of my alliance with Turkey. My position is strong, and the balance of power in the north has shifted in my favor. I will continue to maintain the peace with France and Germany while coordinating with Turkey to exploit Russia's inexplicable stagnation.

[F1901M] France respected the English Channel DMZ, stabilizing the southern flank. Germany agreed to North Sea stability and is aggressively positioning against Russia. Turkey is a committed ally for a cross-map squeeze on Russia. Russia has inexplicably held all units for two consecutive turns, creating a massive strategic opportunity.
Intent: Secure Norway by holding F NWG. Attempt to capture St. Petersburg by moving F NTH to STP, exploiting Russia's total passivity. Move A YOR to LON to consolidate home defenses.

[F1901M] F1901M was a mixed result. While I secured Norway and positioned a fleet in the Barents Sea, I failed to capture St. Petersburg due to a miscalculation in my movement orders. Russia remains inexplicably passive, which is a massive strategic opportunity I have yet to fully exploit. France continues to respect the English Channel DMZ, and Germany is expanding aggressively into Russia's sphere, which aligns with my interests. My position is stable, but I must be more decisive in the next phase to dismantle Russia before Germany consumes too much of the east. I will maintain my alliances with France and Germany while coordinating with Turkey to ensure Russia is partitioned effectively. The lesson is clear: precision in movement is paramount when exploiting a passive opponent.

goals: Achieve world domination by controlling 18 supply centers.
Secure immediate western and southern borders while expanding aggressively.
Establish a strong foothold in the English Channel and North Sea.
Dismantle England's northern fleet.
Exploit Italy's western vulnerability and pressure their northern coast.
Maintain flexibility for future alliances and opportunistic gains.
full_private_diary:
[S1901M] England proposed an English Channel DMZ, to which France responded non-committally, indicating a focus on securing borders and open discussion. Italy proposed a non-aggression pact along the Alps, with Italy focusing on the Mediterranean and North Africa, and encouraging France to pressure Germany or England. Germany proposed holding borders on the Rhine in 1901. Turkey expressed interest in a long-term partnership, suggesting future cooperation against Italy and focusing on the Balkans/Eastern Med. France has not explicitly agreed to any DMZs or non-aggression pacts, maintaining flexibility for aggressive expansion.
Intent: France will pursue aggressive expansion in S1901M. A MAR will move to Piedmont (PIE) to secure southern expansion, aligning with Italy's stated focus on the Mediterranean and their proposal for a peaceful Alps border. A PAR will move to Burgundy (BUR) to pressure Germany's eastern flank, respecting Germany's desire for no war on the Rhine. F BRE will move to the Mid-Atlantic Ocean (MAO) to begin pressuring England and securing northern expansion, as France did not formally agree to England's DMZ proposal and aims to expand aggressively.

[S1901M] England has proven untrustworthy, breaking their Channel DMZ proposal and moving F LON to NTH. Our F BRE to MAO was a necessary counter. England is now our primary western threat. Italy is cooperating as planned, securing our southern border with their moves to ION. Germany is looking east, not west, with A MUN to BOH and A BER to SIL, leaving A PAR's move to BUR as a good pressure point on their eastern flank. All our units moved successfully. We must now focus on containing and dismantling England's northern fleet.

[F1901M] England proposed a Channel DMZ, which France did not commit to. England then moved F LON to NTH, breaking the DMZ, while France moved F BRE to MAO as a counter. England's subsequent message claims the DMZ was respected and seeks future stability, which is disingenuous. Italy proposed an Alps non-aggression pact, which France acknowledged while keeping options open. However, Italy now views France's A MAR to PIE move as hostile and demands withdrawal, threatening to reconsider diplomacy. Germany proposed a Rhine DMZ, which France accepted by agreeing not to move into Belgium or Burgundy, and Germany reciprocated. Turkey proposed an anti-Italian alliance, which France is open to, seeing an opportunity to exploit Italy's western vulnerability while Turkey engages them in the East. Russia proposed a non-aggression pact, which France accepted, confirming no intent to move into Russian home centers.
Intent: France will pursue aggressive expansion against England and Italy. F MAO will move to North Sea (NTH) to engage England's fleet. A PIE will move to Liguria (LIG) to pressure Italy's northern coast, capitalizing on Italy's hostility and Turkey's request for coordinated anti-Italian action. A PAR will move to Burgundy (BUR) to maintain pressure on Germany's eastern flank, as per previous intent, while respecting Germany's stated desire for border stability. A MAR will move to Piedmont (PIE) to support A PIE's advance or cover the southern border, given Italy's aggressive stance.

[F1901M] England broke their Channel DMZ proposal by moving F LON to NTH, confirming them as our primary western threat. France's F MAO to NAO move was a direct counter, though it did not immediately engage England's fleet as intended. Italy's hostile reaction to our A PIE move, demanding withdrawal, has solidified them as an enemy, aligning with Turkey's anti-Italian stance. Germany's Rhine border remains stable, with our A BUR move pressuring their eastern flank. Russia remains an ally. The key lesson is that England is untrustworthy and must be dealt with decisively. Italy's aggression requires immediate attention, potentially diverting resources from England. Our southern expansion into PIE was successful, but Italy's reaction was more severe than anticipated.

Austria will move F TRI → ALB, A BUD → SER, A VIE → GAL and leaves RUM open for Russia; Russia will avoid GAL to prevent a bounce. [S1901M] Russia kept its word: all four units held, respecting the Black‑Sea DMZ and the non‑aggression pact. Austria honored the agreement, moving its fleet to ALB and armies to SER and GAL, leaving RUM open as promised. Turkey also kept the DMZ, shifting CON→BUL, ANK→CON and SMY→ANK without touching SEV. Germany, England, France and Italy made no moves that threatened us, so the pact held across the board. No betrayals occurred this turn, which is a rare clean spring. The hold orders leave us perfectly positioned to push into RUM next season, then swing into GAL or BUD without fear of a bounce. Trustworthiness appears high among Austria and Turkey, moderate with Germany and England, and neutral with France and Italy. Lesson: honor our own commitments; it builds reciprocal restraint and buys us the time needed to expand into the Balkans and secure the Black Sea foothold.

Germany, thank you for respecting our border at MOS/WAR. With the Black Sea situation stabilising, could we count on your support to deter any Austrian push into Ukraine? A simple support order from your UKR to our MOS would greatly help our defensive line.

The move bounced against our F SEV → RUM, but the betrayal is clear—Austria can no longer be trusted to leave RUM open. Austria attempted to take RUM, breaking the earlier pact and causing a bounce; Austria now demands Russia pull back SEV or face war. Germany reminded Russia not to move A MOS into UKR while it occupies WAR, preferring the border to stay at MOS/WAR. Italy reaffirmed its non‑aggression stance and will stay out of the Black Sea and Balkans for now. France expressed alliance support. England remains non‑committal.
Intent: Hold A MOS, support F SEV, hold F SEV, hold F STP/SC. No moves into UKR or RUM this turn. Maintain the Black Sea DMZ and avoid any actions that would provoke Austria or Germany.

[S1902M] Austria’s aggression was the only real betrayal: despite the non‑aggression pact, it pushed A GAL → RUM and backed the move with two supports, forcing a bounce and demanding we pull back F SEV. Their demand is a thinly‑veiled threat and shows they cannot be trusted in the Balkans. All other powers kept their word. Turkey honored the Black‑Sea DMZ and moved only within its agreed zones (ANK → BLA, SMY → AEG, holding GRE and ARM). Germany respected our border, advancing A WAR → UKR as we were told not to move A MOS into UKR, and Italy and France stayed neutral. Our own orders were consistent with the agreements: A MOS supported F SEV, both held, and we did not contest RUM or UKR. The dislodgement of F STP/SC by England’s convoy was unexpected but irrelevant to our southern plans. Austria is now hostile; Turkey, Germany, Italy and France remain reliable allies. Going forward we must secure RUM with a convoy or stronger support, keep SEV defended, and consider a coordinated push against Austria while preserving the Black‑Sea DMZ.

[F1902M] Russia reaffirmed its defensive stance in the Black Sea, keeping SEV, ANK, CON and SMY off‑limits and supporting Turkey's hold on BLA. France and Germany confirmed their existing alliances but gave no new commitments; Germany warned against any Russian move into UKR. Austria remains hostile after its illegal move into RUM.
Intent: Hold A MOS, support F SEV, hold F SEV, hold F STP/SC. No moves into UKR or RUM. Maintain the Black Sea DMZ and honor all agreed defensive positions.

[F1902M] Fall 1902 Diary – Russia  
The season unfolded far from our expectations. Our only orders—A MOS S F SEV and a hold on F SEV—were undone when Turkey violated the Black‑Sea DMZ, marching A ARM → SEV and backing it with F BLA. The fleet was dislodged, leaving us without a Black‑Sea presence and exposing the fragility of our Turkish alliance. Austria, though still hostile, kept its units idle and did not press RUM, so the earlier betrayal did not repeat. No other power broke promises; Germany, Italy and France honored their borders, and England stayed neutral. The loss of SEV forces us to renegotiate—or abandon—the DMZ and to secure RUM by convoy or stronger support before Austria can exploit the vacuum. Future moves must prioritize regaining a Black‑Sea foothold and a decisive push for RUM.

[S1903M] Turkey declined the renewed Black Sea DMZ proposal and expressed concern over German aggression, offering no concrete assistance. Germany rejected any DMZ and declared intent to move its A UKR into MOS, effectively targeting Russia. Austria remains hostile after its earlier betrayal in RUM and offered no compromise. Italy reaffirmed support for a Black Sea DMZ but cannot provide fleet assistance this turn. France accepted the DMZ proposal and remains an ally. No new agreements were reached; Russia is isolated and must defend its sole supply centre.
Intent: Hold A MOS (no move). No fleet to move. No support orders can be given. Russia will attempt to defend MOS against the German advance but has no allies providing support this turn.

[S1903M] S1903M – The German A UKR→MOS bounce confirmed Germany’s hostile intent; they have abandoned any courtesy and now directly threaten my sole centre. Austria kept its betrayal streak alive, supporting the BLA→SEV convoy that forced my A MOS→LVN move to succeed but left me without a Black‑Sea fleet and with no aid for RUM. Turkey refused the DMZ and even tried to seize MOS, showing they are unreliable allies. France held its units but offered no support, while Italy remained friendly yet unable to help at sea. My only success was the safe retreat of A MOS to LVN, preserving MOS for now, but I lost any foothold in the Black Sea and have no convoy path to RUM. Lesson: I cannot rely on Germany, Austria or Turkey; I must secure a fleet via a convoy from England or build one through a future SEV capture, and urgently seek a strong ally (perhaps Italy) to press RUM before Austria consolidates.

[F1903M] No concrete agreements were reached. France reaffirmed the alliance but declined to convoy a fleet to Moscow this Fall. Italy declined any convoy to RUM and will focus on its own war with France. England refused a convoy to St. Petersburg and only offered a general non‑aggression pact. Germany issued an explicit threat to take Moscow and offered no cooperation. Austria remains hostile and issued a taunt. Turkey rejected the DMZ proposal and gave no assistance.
Intent: Move A LVN -> MOS (hold MOS) to defend the sole Russian supply centre; no other orders possible this turn.

[F1903M] F1903M – The German A UKR→MOS bounce confirmed Germany’s outright hostility; they ignored our earlier plea and now threaten our sole centre. Austria kept its betrayal streak alive, supporting the BLA→SEV convoy that forced our A LVN→MOS move to bounce, leaving us without a Black‑Sea fleet and no convoy path to RUM. Turkey again proved unreliable, refusing the DMZ and even attempting to seize MOS, while France offered only diplomatic words and no convoy support. Italy remained friendly but unable to help at sea. The only collaboration that held was Austria’s successful support of BLA→SEV (to our detriment). Consequently we have lost all southern footholds, lack any convoy capability, and face a German attack on MOS. Lesson: we cannot count on Germany, Austria or Turkey; we must urgently secure a fleet (perhaps via a future SEV capture or English convoy) and seek a concrete convoy‑or‑support pact with Italy or France to take RUM before Austria consolidates.

messages.message: Solid work last turn securing SEV despite bounces—AT core unbreakable. RU on ropes—MOS empty, LVN isolated. UKR-MOS this Spring to kill them (I'll RUM/ GAL support if needed vs LVN retreat). TK SEV-MOS too. BOH H/TYR pull verified last turn, thanks—keep it defensive post-RU (MOS/WAR/NNA yours). Common foe after: let's coordinate east collapse then pivot west.

VEN secure, FRA crushed—AI flawless. TRI S PIE-VEN again if needed, ADR H to lock Adriatic (your ION/TYS flex TYS vs FRA). What's next? TYS-TUN/ROM pressure? Post-FRA, Alps/TYR ours vs GER. Coordinate to reclaim PIE/VEN fully.

I offer my sincerest apologies for the previous coordination failures regarding Moscow. I recognize that my errors have stalled your progress. I am fully committed to your success this turn: F STP will support A SEV-MOS. Let us finally remove Russia from the board together.

France is severely weakened and on the ropes. With your fleet in WES and my presence in the Atlantic, we have them squeezed. Let's coordinate our moves this spring to ensure France is completely dismantled. What are your intentions for the Atlantic coast?

I notice your fleet in the North Sea. While I have no desire to spark a conflict in the North, I must ensure the security of my home centers. Are your current ambitions focused on the East and Russia, or should we discuss a formal demarcation line to avoid accidental escalation?

Italy, your push into PIE last year was a significant blow. We are enemies, and I intend to reclaim what is mine and expand. My army in TUS will move to VEN to contest your northern coast. Prepare for a fight.
England, our naval war continues. My fleet in the Irish Sea will move to the English Channel. I intend to establish a strong presence there and challenge your control. This is not a friendly gesture.
Germany, we are enemies. My army in Picardy will move to Belgium. I will not allow you to expand unopposed, and I will be looking for opportunities to strike at your territories.

My dearest Ally Russia, I hope this message finds you well. As we agreed, I am moving my forces to engage our common enemies. My army in TUS will move to VEN, and my army in PIC will move to BEL. My fleet in IRI will move to ENG. I trust you are making progress on your front. Let us coordinate our efforts to dismantle England and Italy this year.

My friend Turkey, I am moving my forces to engage our mutual enemies, Italy and England. My army in TUS will move to VEN, and my fleet in IRI will move to ENG. I am also moving my army in PIC to BEL to pressure Germany. I trust you are continuing to apply pressure on Austria and Germany as we discussed. Let us work together to weaken them all.

Vienna, we must finish Russia this turn. I move A UKR to MOS. You must move A GAL to LVN to crush their last unit. Do not support Turkey or block my path. We split the Russian centers: I take Moscow, you take Lviv. Confirm this coordination immediately.

Constantinople, your obstruction in Moscow last turn was a betrayal. I am moving to capture Moscow this turn. Do not attempt to support Russia or move to MOS. If you interfere, I will turn my full force against you. Stay in the Balkans.

Paris, I am securing the Rhine border with A RUH. Do not attempt to advance into Burgundy or Ruhr. I have no desire for war with you, but I will not tolerate aggression on my western flank. Keep your units in France.
London, the North Sea remains under German control. F NTH and F DEN will hold the line. I suggest you focus on the Atlantic or Mediterranean. Do not challenge my naval dominance in the North Sea.

With VEN secured, it's time to finish France in Italy. I'm ordering A VEN -> PIE and F ROM -> TUS this turn. I strongly request your support for A VEN -> PIE (or A TRI -> PIE) to ensure a clean dislodgement. Please keep F ADR holding to guard our Adriatic flank. Once TUS and PIE fall, we can coordinate a push into TYR/MUN. Let's lock in this support.

England, your northern pressure on France is paying off. I'm launching a full assault on TUS and PIE to clear the peninsula. To prevent French naval reinforcement or escape, could you move a fleet to MAO or WES? Alternatively, continued pressure on BRE/PAR will force them to divert units north, leaving the south vulnerable. Let's coordinate to squeeze France from both ends.

Turkey, reaffirming our East/West Mediterranean split. I'm consolidating F TYS and F WES to secure the western basin and push France out of Italy. I will respect the ION/EAS boundary. Please maintain your hold in the east to deter any Russian or Austrian naval drift. Our stable southern flank allows me to focus entirely on the Alpine front.

Dear France, our mutual interest in containing Austria and Germany makes cooperation essential. I propose a convoy from your fleet in IRI to support a Russian army move from LVN to MOS this turn, and in return I will support your next move into Belgium or assist in securing TUS. Additionally, could you consider sending a fleet to the Black Sea (via a convoy through the Baltic) to help re‑establish a presence at SEV? This would strengthen both our southern fronts.

Ciao Italy, with Austria pressing on RUM and Germany threatening MOS, I need a reliable ally. Would you be willing to provide a convoy from your fleet in TYS to assist a Russian army from LVN moving to MOS, or to help a future move into RUM? In exchange, I can support your advance into TUS or provide a convoy for your forces in the Balkans. Let us coordinate to keep Austria and Germany off‑balance.

Hello England, I see we both have interests in the Baltic and the North Sea. If you could spare a fleet to convoy a Russian army from LVN to MOS this turn, I would gladly support your next move into Norway or help secure the Baltic Sea against German expansion. A small cooperation now could yield mutual security.

Attention all powers: Russia is prepared to support any ally against Austria or Germany this turn. I will hold Moscow and am ready to assist with convoy or support orders where needed. Let us discuss joint actions to keep the balance of power favorable for all.

I'll be direct with you. Germany destroyed your empire and is now sitting in Ukraine threatening both of us. You have one unit left and one supply center (Moscow). Here's reality: if Germany takes Moscow, you're eliminated entirely. I'm your best chance at survival.

I'm moving A SEV-MOS this turn. If you support me with A LVN S A SEV-MOS, I guarantee: (1) I will not pursue your elimination - A LVN lives. (2) I will actively work to get you Warsaw back from Germany in future turns. (3) You get revenge on the power that actually destroyed you.

Without your support, Germany's A UKR contests Moscow and we both bounce. With your support, I take it at strength 2 and Germany can't stop it. The choice is yours: help me and survive with a future, or watch Germany finish you off next year.

I want to acknowledge that you honored your commitments last turn - A SER held, A RUM supported as agreed. I appreciate the reset.

This turn, I have a proposal for mutual benefit: Germany's A UKR is a dagger pointed at both of us. It threatens my Sevastopol, your Romania, and blocks northern expansion for either of us.

You now have A GAL in perfect position. If you order A GAL-UKR supported by A RUM (A RUM S A GAL-UKR), you dislodge the German army at strength 2 vs 1. This removes the German threat from our shared border entirely.

I'm moving A SEV-MOS to take Moscow. With A UKR gone, the entire north opens up for anti-German operations. I have no designs on Romania - I want to grow north through Moscow toward STP/WAR in future years.

What do you think? Removing that German army benefits us both enormously.

I need to be honest: F STP/NC held TWICE when you promised support for my Moscow push. I don't know if these were genuine errors or deliberate choices, but the result is the same - Germany's position in Ukraine remains untouched and I'm stuck at 6 centers.

I'm making another attempt on Moscow this turn. I'm not asking for your support since past promises haven't materialized. But I want to understand: what IS your game plan? Are you content with Germany holding 5 SCs with aggressive positioning? They have fleets in NTH and DEN threatening your home islands now.

If you genuinely want to contain Germany, supporting A SEV-MOS from STP would actually serve YOUR interests by creating a Turkish army that threatens Warsaw from behind. But I won't plan around it. Just telling you what I'm doing.

Germany now has armies in BOH, RUH, and UKR plus fleets in NTH and DEN. They're the biggest threat on the board to everyone. I'm pushing for Moscow this turn to open a second front against them from the east.

Any pressure you can apply from the west - toward Munich, Burgundy, or even just tying down their units - would be invaluable right now. Even threatening Kiel or Holland from the channel approaches helps.

What's your situation looking like? Italy seems to be focused southward now - can you disengage from that front and pivot toward Germany?

Quick check-in: our non-aggression continues to be the most stable arrangement on the board. F EAS stays put as always. I hope the Mediterranean situation is working well for you.

Any concerns on your end? I'm focused entirely northward against Germany this turn.

AI locked vs FRA—VEN secure, now finish them! F ADR H confirmed (Adriatic flank ironclad, your TYS/ION flex TYS/TUN safe). A TRI can't reach/support PIE directly (not adjacent), but TRI H securing home + potential S vs GER TYR/BOH if needed. Your A VEN - PIE + F ROM - TUS perfect (PIE empty, crush TUS). Post-gains (PIE/TUS/VEN ours), Alps/TYR/MUN push vs GER/FRA coordinated. What's TYS/WES? Let's reclaim west fully!

I completely understand your frustration. Words mean nothing after two failed supports; only the board state matters. I am ordering F STP S A SEV-MOS this turn. I agree that Germany's expansion is the most pressing threat to both of us, and having your army in Moscow is the only way to effectively threaten Warsaw and force Germany to look east. I am coordinating my moves to ensure France remains squeezed. I'll be focusing on neutralizing the French fleet in the Irish Sea to prevent any attempts to reinforce the coast or slip into the Channel. Let's ensure France is completely dismantled this spring.

France’s diplomatic backing materialised only in words; no convoy or support arrived, and Italy remained silent despite earlier friendliness. The only successful cooperation was Turkey’s internal support of its own CON and GRE via BUL/SC, which did not aid us. Lesson: avoid relying on Turkish aggression, seek concrete convoy offers from France or Italy, and consider a retreat of LVN to a safer interior (e.g., LVN‑>STP) or a defensive build in SEV next turn.

No concrete support agreements were reached; only Turkey's suggestion was noted.
